plan.title: bug(scope): scope:complete's printed delivery-identity-attest remedy is unreachable; story-line marks and orphan check trap stories

narratives.Description: scope:complete refuses a product PR that carried deft-story-part on every basis and prints an operator-attestation command that the join never reads, so shipped stories cannot complete (seven in deftai/evolution, #6882 item 1). This story makes printed remedies reachable, opens a guarded basis (d) route for a part-line product PR on the scope:complete command only, and reports a shipped brief as pending while its lifecycle PR is open.
narratives.Overview:
1. Remedy argument (P1). `refuse()` in `proveIssueAnchoredAssociation` (`packages/core/src/scope/delivery-evidence.ts`) takes the remedy as an argument instead of always appending the attestation command. The command is the remedy only when this run would accept basis (d) if a usable grant were present: the merge-time body was read; the PR has no sole `deft-story: N` mark (or it is on the item 3 route with its sibling check held); no earlier read in this run failed; the plan has an id; the attestation lookup is wired and its store resolved; `candidateDeliveryRefusal` passed; and the lookup found no usable grant. An expired unused grant counts as no usable grant: its re-mint and `authz:revoke` text is shown only under those same conditions. To make that possible, `proveAttestedBasis` runs `candidateDeliveryRefusal` before it uses the lookup's reason.
2. Other remedies (P1). A failed read (merge-time body, forge unwired, uniqueness scan, delivery-branch stamp, connection events, changed files, open-PR list) says which read failed and to retry. A zero-file or brief-and-CHANGELOG-only PR says it is not a delivery and to run `scope:complete` with the story's product PR (`--pr <n> --merge-commit <sha>`); that is the whole remedy, with or without a grant, expired or not. A contested sole mark names the other marked PRs and `metadata.productPullRequest` on the fetched delivery branch. A missing plan id names the brief. An unresolved grant store names the store error. The refusals that already return outside `refuse()` (repository mismatch, missing PR number, unmerged PR, merge-commit mismatch) are unchanged.
3. Part-line route (P2). The join input gets one optional field, `partLineAttestation`. Only the `scope:complete` command entry (`packages/core/src/scope/main.ts`) sets it; the shared transition defaults it to off, so `completeCohort`, `swarm:finalize-cohort` and the lands-with-product tip proof keep today's part-line refusal. With it, a part-line body runs no basis but (d), and only after a sibling check holds. A "product part" is a PR whose diff has at least one path outside the brief-land family (`isDeliveryBriefLandPath`) and outside `.deft/`. The check: (i) the candidate is a product part; (ii) the merged-PR scan (`scanSoleMarkCompetitors`) completes, finds no sole-mark competitor, and every other part-line PR it records is not a product part (activation, mint, widen and other brief-only or `.deft/`-only PRs never block); (iii) a separate open-PR list completes: every open pull request whose base repository is this repository, fork heads included, paged until a short page; no body in it carries `deft-story: N`, and every open pull request whose body carries `deft-story-part: N` is not a product part (its changed files, paged, decide; activation, mint and other brief-only or `.deft/`-only open PRs never block). If the check holds, a usable grant completes the story with basis `operator-attested`, and without one the refusal prints that PR's attestation command (item 1). If it fails, the refusal names the blocking PRs and says to complete with a PR that carries `deft-story: N`. A failed scan, a failed changed-file read of a merged or open sibling, or a failed, short-stopped or unparseable open-PR list is a retry remedy and never completes. A body with both lines keeps today's pre-merge refusal and is not offered the command.
4. Contract (P2). `content/contracts/human-origin-authz.md` rows Admission and Keep-outs: a part-line PR is admitted only on the `scope:complete` command under the item 3 sibling check; it is never a finalize close; the contested-sole-mark keep-out stays. The part-line refusal text in `delivery-evidence.ts` (1993-2003) is replaced by the item 3 outcomes.
5. Orphan pending (P3). In `packages/core/src/orphan-active/evaluate.ts`, after the brief loop and only when at least one brief is `shipped`, list open PRs with REST `pulls?state=open&per_page=100`, paged until a short page. For this match only, keep PRs whose head repository is this repository. For each, read its changed files (paged). A shipped brief is pending when one of those PRs moves that exact `xbrief/active/<file>` to `xbrief/completed/<file>`: a rename, or a removal of the active path beside an add of the completed path. A pending brief leaves the failing list; the run's message names the PR (`pending lifecycle PR #M`). Any failed, unparseable or incomplete list or file read keeps every shipped verdict. The issue number in the PR body is not the selector. `unresolved`, `dropped-ref` and `lands-with-product-unproven` are unchanged.
6. Unchanged: bases (a), (b), (c), brief-in-PR-diff and their order on the non-part path; the contested-sole-mark settlement by the delivery-branch stamp; finalize's mark scan (`parseAllDeftStoryMarks` ignores the part line); the `--changed-only` merge chokepoint on feature branches; `verify:completed-tracked`; the pre-merge story-line checks in `pr-closing-keywords/main.ts`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a merged part-line product PR, no other merged part-line product part of the story, no sole-mark competitor, no open PR on this repository's base carrying a story line for N, and a matching `delivery-identity-attest` grant, when `scope:complete --pr <it> --merge-commit <sha>` runs, then the story completes with basis `operator-attested`.
- Given the same PR without a grant, then `scope:complete` refuses and prints that PR's attestation command; after the operator mints it, the next run completes.
- Given the same PR while a merged activation PR (brief only) and a merged intent-constraint mint PR (`.deft/` only) of the story both carry `deft-story-part: N`, or an open brief-only or `.deft/`-only PR (fork or this repository) carries `deft-story-part: N`, then the route still holds.
- Given the same PR while an open PR from a fork, or from this repository, carries `deft-story: N`, or another open or merged product part (fork or this repository) carries `deft-story-part: N`, then the refusal names that PR and prints no attestation command.
- Given the same part-line PR through `swarm:finalize-cohort --pr <it> --stories N`, then it is refused as today, grant or not.
- Given a brief-only PR with a sole `deft-story: N` mark (the #6639 shape), or a brief-only PR with no story line and an expired grant, then the refusal says it is not a delivery, names the product-PR remedy, and prints no attestation or re-mint command.
- Given a PR with no story line whose connection-events read fails, or whose plan has no id, then the refusal names that cause and prints no attestation command.
- Given an active brief whose issue is closed, when an open same-repository PR renames that brief into `xbrief/completed/`, then `verify:orphan-active -- --issue N` and the delivery-tip sweep exit 0 and name the pending PR; the same holds for a removal beside an add.
- Given the same brief when the matching PR is from a fork, is closed, or the open-PR list fails or stops early, then the run still reports it as shipped and exits 1.

## In plain English
Story #6601 shipped in product PR #6610, whose body said `deft-story-part: 6601`. A part line means "this PR does not complete the story", and `scope:complete` refuses such a PR on every basis, operator attestation included. A later brief-only PR (#6639) carried `deft-story: 6601`, but a PR that changes only briefs is not a delivery, so it fails too. The refusal for #6639 printed an attestation command for #6639. The operator minted it, and the same refusal came back, because a PR with the sole mark never reaches the attestation check, and the attestation would fail the delivery check anyway. Nothing completes #6601. Separately, after a product PR merges and its issue is closed, `verify:orphan-active` fails on the still-active brief while the lifecycle PR that moves it is open; the workarounds were reopening the issue, or merging that PR by hand. The recommended fix lets the existing attestation recover a part-line PR, prints the attestation command only where it can work, and lets the orphan check pass a brief whose lifecycle PR is open.

## Pains
#6645 has no Acceptance Criteria heading. These three pains are derived from its Summary, Evidence and Expected sections.
- P1 — `scope:complete` prints the `delivery-identity-attest` command on refusals that never read that grant, or where the grant could never be admitted: a sole-mark PR whose mark proof fails ("(d) not evaluated"), and a PR that fails the delivery checks the attestation also needs (a brief-only PR). A minted grant then changes nothing (#6601 / #6639).
- P2 — A story whose product PR merged with `deft-story-part: N` has no sanctioned completion route: the part line refuses every basis, attestation included, and a brief-only follow-up PR with `deft-story: N` is excluded as non-delivery (#6601 / #6610).
- P3 — After the product PR merges and the issue is closed, `verify:orphan-active` reports the still-active brief as shipped while the lifecycle PR that moves it to `completed/` is open, so the after-merge check and the delivery-tip sweep fail until a human merges that PR (#6599 / #6636).

## Constraints (not pains)
- Add no gate and no grant kind. Prefer the smallest rule; a fix removes a step or a refusal.
- Not a pain of this arc: choosing the mark at PR open. A PR-open check of the mark adds a gate; once a wrong part line is recoverable (P2), the mark choice stops being a trap. A part line on a brief-only PR is #6544 and stays there.
- A part line is still never a finalize close signal and never completes a story on bases (a), (b), (c) or brief-in-PR-diff.
- `verify:completed-tracked` is unchanged: DONE still waits for the completed brief to land.
- Running stories not to overlap: #6480 (`hooks/scope.ts`, `hooks/dispatcher.ts`, `scope/lands-with-product.ts`, `policy/write-fence.ts`), #6477 (design-critique gate, intake ingest).

Problem: story #6601 shipped in product PR #6610, which carried `deft-story-part: 6601`. `scope:complete` refuses a part-line PR on every basis, operator attestation included, and the brief-only follow-up PR with `deft-story: 6601` is not a delivery. ## Summary

Lead finding: **the remedy that `scope:complete` prints is unreachable.** For #6601 the printed remedy is a `delivery-identity-attest` grant on #6639@cff0e85c3. The operator minted that grant, and `scope:complete` still refuses with the same text. The text says "(d) not evaluated: the PR carries the sole mark; settle the mark instead". So the check stops at basis (a) and never reads the grant it told the operator to mint.

Two related lifecycle traps follow from the story-line marks and the orphan check.

## Evidence

Story-line mark trap (#6601):
- Product PR #6610 carried `deft-story-part: 6601`. `scope:complete` says a partial delivery "cannot complete the story on any basis, operator attestation included".
- Brief-only PR #6639 carries `deft-story: 6601`, but it is excluded as non-delivery.
- The grant minted on #6639@cff0e85c3 is never evaluated (see the lead finding). No sanctioned route completes the story.
- Workers cannot tell which mark a PR needs. Activation, mint and widen PRs take `-part`; product PRs take `deft-story`. Using `-part` on the product PR is what made #6601 uncompletable. (Related: #6544.)

Orphan check on a closed issue:
- `verify:orphan-active` flags a closed issue whose brief is still active. Fixing it means reopening the issue or folding completion into the same PR (seen on #6599 after #6607 merged and before lifecycle PR #6636).

## Expected

- A printed remedy must be reachable: if `scope:complete` names a grant, it evaluates that grant, or it names a different remedy.
- The mark a PR needs is derived from its role, or checked at PR open with a clear message, instead of failing at completion.
- The orphan check allows the closed-issue and active-brief window while a lifecycle PR for that brief is open.
- Prefer removing a step over adding a gate.

## Workaround used today

None for #6601 (still stuck; the operator minted the grant and it was ignored). For #6599, waited for lifecycle PR #6636 and merged it by hand.

Given a PR with no story line whose connection-events read fails, or whose plan has no id, then the refusal names that cause and prints no attestation command.

Given an active brief whose issue is closed, when an open same-repository PR renames that brief into `xbrief/completed/`, then `verify:orphan-active -- --issue N` and the delivery-tip sweep exit 0 and name the pending PR; the same holds for a removal beside an add.
Given the same brief when the matching PR is from a fork, is closed, or the open-PR list fails or stops early, then the run still reports it as shipped and exits 1.
